result.title: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel
result.summary: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated through open channels such as social media, even when the information they receive is truthful. When agents fill gaps between fragments with self-induced relationships, they may accept those relationships as established facts and pass the resulting rumours to others. Drawing on cognitive theory of narrative understanding and film theory of montage, we introduce Generative Montage to operationalize this failure, termed narrative overfitting, by coordinating agents to arrange truthful fragments into misleading narratives. Across 1,090 rumour targets from six Twitter events, agents often accepted rumours overconfidently, with overall acceptance exceeding 65 percent in twelve of fourteen models. Acceptance remained above 50 percent after majority voting or review of the same evidence, showing how errors can reach downstream decisions. To explain this susceptibility, fragment interventions identify posts that influence belief within complete narratives. Synthetic controls then show that similar response patterns arise from valid evidence, separating belief influence from evidential support. This distinction motivates Grounded Monitor, a proof-of-concept neuro-symbolic runtime monitor that checks direct evidential support to guide agents' judgements, improving decision accuracy by 5.6 to 29.0 percentage points across original and anonymized settings. These findings expose a cognitive route to rumour amplification and support monitoring inferred relationships before agent-generated conclusions guide public decisions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究语言模型智能体如何把真实信息片段拼接成误导性叙事并产生 narrative overfitting，通过 Generative Montage 在多起谣言事件上量化其过度自信接受，并提出检查直接证据支持的运行时监控器 Grounded Monitor。
AI.relevance_reason: 其区分「直接证据支持」与「推断关系造成的信念影响」的监控思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 推断是否有证据支撑及何时应停止或回退到显式证据，但该工作并非视觉多模态研究，需进一步检查迁移可行性。
